Metaphor feels like the Persona team was told to make a game that's not Persona, but only know how to make Persona games. That's not a knock against the game. It's very well made, but P5's design philosophy permeates every aspect of the game. From the menu and battle UI, to the Bonds (Social Links) and Archetypes (Personas (Even though it's more like a FF Job system)), Metaphor has a bit of difficulty carving out it's own identity from behind the shadow of P5. Even the social commentary is just as forced. That said, if you enjoy persona, and I certainly do, Metaphor is an excellent game to scratch that itch while we wait for P6.

Before Metaphor:
P3 - best story
P4 - best cast
P5 - best gameplay

After Metaphor:
Metaphor best everything! + best pacing

Just completed my first play through. Completing A LOT of side content and not rushing the story took me 93 hours. That's a testament to how great the game is itself.

The game follows the calendar format of the persona games which is NOT a bad thing but it has its own system when it comes to enemies, archetypes etc. There's a lot you can unlock as far as archetypes which is like the persona for those that are familiar with that series. You can freely change your archetype which is such a fantastic system. You need to grind for them but they're worth it.

The story was actually remarkably well written. The plot twists caught me off guard which is very hard to do. The side quests are very well fleshed out and they provide a lot of context to the world and enemies. The map is also MASSIVE so there will be a lot of side quests leading to areas you haven't discovered yet which is also very nice. You can try to rush the story without leveling up your squad but I promise you, you'll quickly hit a wall.

Game also has a NG+ feature which provides a ton of replayability. I recommend picking it up. Hoping they add story DLC in the future but it's not NEEDED, more of a want.

The art and UI is one of my favorite from an Atlus game or a RPG in general. Also, the background music was really nice, I almost never play with volume in games but I definitely had that BGM high. The story is pretty decent, while having some cliche tropes (but it uses them well). I contrast to a lot of SMT games, it at least shows progress being made in a epilogue. Restarting a fight was a nice mechanic, makes trying to learn weakness less of a punishment.

My biggest issue (and this has been across a lot of the SMT games with press turn) is status effects are almost never useful. At least there is some dungeons where it has uses, but even with high luck I could barely get them to proc. I'm hoping they improve them in future games, maybe only has a pip is removed if no status is inflected.

Metaphor: ReFantazio was a game that genuinely surprised me. After being a recent Persona fan, I was interested in this new game as it takes a lot of elements we love from Persona into this game, but this game felt unique somehow despite the gameplay similarities. It takes a concept of a "fantasy" and if we can make things of what we want, a reality. The themes and nature of the story can be very dark but I was moved with the story and its optimism. The cast themselves are great, each with backstories that are genuine with great development. It was to the point where I thought to myself, I didn't want this adventure to end with them. However, after finishing, I can genuinely say that not only did this game rise to one of my favorite games of all time, it had, in my opinion, one of best villains of all time along with one of the more satisfying endings as well. If you like Persona and just like JRPGs in general, you'll love this one. It's filled with twists and turns with a familiar format yet incredible presentation inside of the game. You may also learn a lot too and maybe even ask the question yourself, maybe if you are going through something, how can you make things better in your life and for everyone around you? This story helps you learn that and might even motivate you. Incredible game.

A must play challenging JRPG, which makes you think and strategise before each fight zone. The game is not that "perfect" as there are more that it needs to have, but the visual, craziness, strategising and unique novelty aspect which other JRPG does not have; makes up for it.

Although it is similar to Persona series, it is a unique playthrough experience.
It does not have:
- Romance
- Collecting aspects
- Unique "All strike" mechanics

But it makes it up with:
- Combination of multiple skills strategies
- Crazy weird bosses
- Protagonist has their own voice!!
- Difficulty challenging, squeezes out every point of to develop your protagonist or should you grind; Both are worthy decision to increase your team strength.

Absolutely, utterly fantastic. Every single part of this game is crafted extremely well. The gameplay is a refinement of Atlus' already great previous works. Every piece of music is grandiose and memorable. The designs, from the characters to the Archetypes to the environments, are impeccable. The voice acting is full of life and makes every character gripping. Any faults the game has are minor nitpicks and few and far between. Above that all though, is that it's a really genuine fantasy story that doesn't try to wag you about being fantasy or try to shoehorn in any 'modern' magical elements. I think this is a quintessential pick for any RPG fan and possibly one of my favorite games of all time.

Not really sure why this game is so highly rated, the characters are so generic and similar that I couldn't tell you one personality trait that Strohl and Hulkenberg don't share, the tone of the story is so strange and inconsistent, and the levelling system is one of the worst implementations I've ever seen. For instance, I made my Hulkenberg a knight and gunner so I could deal decent damage from the back and draw aggro, but it turns out that chose wrong, and in order to get the higher levels of knight I need mage levels, so I just wasted all that exp on gunner and now I am forced to make her a mage/knight. The ability to customise your team comps is simply non-existent, as there's literally one 1 path for each character to take, which the game doesn't even tell you, you have to google it.
(5/10 simply because it is a high quality product, with MAJOR flaws that ruin the game)

Honestly, as a fan of Persona, I wanted to love this so much. But after 10 hours, I just have zero desire to keep going. I know it’s an 80-hour RPG, but a game needs to hook you somewhere in the first 10 hours, and absolutely nothing has happened to pull me in.

The narrative is just flat, and none of the characters have any real charm or personality to hook you. I don't care about the world or the people in it.

The first dungeon is a slog. It drags on way too long. Finishing it felt like a total chore, and it completely killed my motivation to see what comes next.

Combat is passable at best and it gets repetitive fast. On top of that, the Archetype system feels like a terrible, tedious grind just to make progress.

Persona with extra steps, that’s exactly what this feels like, except it misses the magic. The calendar system worked in Persona, but here it feels completely artificial and forced just to check an Atlus box. It feels like a copy-paste job with extra layers of unnecessary friction.

Metaphor accomplishes something that many games that have been released in the last decade have failed or struggled to do: tell a compelling and COMPLETE story within its meager 100+ hour campaign, without the need or ask of paid DLC or extra material. Its story may not be the greatest story ever told, but it is a story told greatly and it's an important one. Despite the cast of characters in the game being various fantasy races, ATLUS tells a story that's an incredibly human and personal experience.
The gameplay and combat are perfectly serviceable to anyone picking up the game. It's simple enough for first time players of the genre to learn, and just complex enough for long time veterans to figure out how to optimize its systems. Though the "job system" is nothing revolutionary to the genre, it fits well thematically and is implemented in a very fun and engaging way.
Metaphor: ReFantazio is a distinctly bright mark in the history of video games, it deserves to be celebrated and is worth your time.
